acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust now allocates and clips the tools outer panel, heading, scrolling form body and history-clear row. Native services retain child measurement, View/window/event/AX/scroll ownership and browser commands. Views retains the original BoxLayout policy.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: SetSidebarPanelLayout selects a Rust allocator in the opt-in backend and the original BoxLayout start/stretch configuration for Views. Four scopes move: vertical outer panel (20px interior, 12px gaps, scroll flex), horizontal header (8px gap, title flex), vertical form body (bottom/right 8px, 10px gaps, no flex), and horizontal clear row (8px gap, period selector flex). Existing row/action/editor/select layouts remain unchanged.

Only native child preferred sizes, margins, visibility/ignore flags, insets, orientation and an optional single flexible child index cross this new ABI. Rust owns natural/flex allocation, zero-child gap handling, main-axis clipping and reported host/child geometry. No native View pointer, window or browser object crosses. This configured start/stretch, noncollapsing, nonnegative-margin/inset allocator is not a general replacement for every BoxLayout alignment/multiple-flex policy.

Native font/control services supply preferred sizes. Shrinking children are remeasured at the allocated bounds; Rust preserves the initial flex budget instead of redistributing space after shrink, matching the original configured policy. The adapter preserves child identity and native layout/event/AX/scroll delivery. Native View/ScrollView containers and outer placement still remain.

Three Rust cases cover viewport/header/footer allocation, shrink/clipping and initial-budget preservation, zero-size children, empty lists, margins and saturating large sizes. A shared browser oracle uses the actual Chromium BoxLayout with independently measured probe views: 24 orientation/flex/visibility/margin configurations times 7 widths and 6 heights (1008 bounded combinations), plus natural/minimum/height-for-width comparisons. Bounds include zero, narrow and odd sizes, wrapping, hidden and ignored children and host borders.

A second shared browser case cycles all four real tools pages at two sizes with long Unicode status, checking header/scroll/footer spacing, wrapping, scroll extent and positive viewport space. The Rust backend also checks actual Metal underlay ordering and editor/dismiss cutouts after scrolling. Existing scene/history/controller/Cocoa behavior remains in the critical and full matrices.

The frozen UI override and source manifest now explicitly include sidebar_layout.cc and sidebar_layout.h. Their prior staged contents matched the live committed versions before this change. Network-policy worktree changes remain outside the isolated candidate.

No rendering recipe, crate/library/dependency, domain validation, store or browser-service operation changed. Root/header/body/clear geometry migration does not remove native container or interaction ownership.
initial_compile_issues: The new Rust implementation was initially inserted beside the FFI declaration rather than the out-of-bridge definition; it was moved before the real implementation.
Chromium requires metadata on typed AddChildView probe classes; the test probe now declares and implements that metadata.

initial_probe.resolution: The actual BoxLayout oracle passed on both backends. The real-panel test incorrectly treated the widget contents wrapper (one child) as the tools panel (three children), failing on both backends. It now locates the actual panel via the scroll ancestor of the real editor; the same geometry, scroll and Metal cutout requirements remain. Production allocator code did not change after that probe.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Native tools View/ScrollView/window/event/focus/AX ownership and placement, other panels/forms and layouts, remaining option-to-field/form construction and service/progress wording remain open. This allocator covers the four configured tools roles, not every arbitrary BoxLayout policy or inherited Chromium UI.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
